response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.dealedge, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS n FROM orders o JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.dealedge), a AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS av FROM c) SELECT SUM(c.n) AS total_count, AVG(c.n - a.av) AS avg_excess FROM c CROSS JOIN a WHERE c.n > a.av

assumptions.assumption: An order is counted once per side even if several risk/margin records match it (COUNT DISTINCT recordvault).
The average is taken across the sides that have at least one matched order, since sides with no matches don't appear. Any NULL dealedge value would count as its own group.
avg_excess is the mean of (side count - average count) over the sides above the average, with no rounding.

alternatives.interpretation: Count matched risk/margin records (joined rows) per side rather than distinct orders.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.dealedge, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders o JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.dealedge), a AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS av FROM c) SELECT SUM(c.n) AS total_count, AVG(c.n - a.av) AS avg_excess FROM c CROSS JOIN a WHERE c.n > a.av
